newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius sees limited cyclone damage to sugarcane. [CORRECTED 16:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Mauritius sees limited cyclone damage to sugarcane. [CORRECTED 16:00 GMT]

text.p: Tropical cyclone Daniella damaged five percent of the sugarcane planted in Mauritius early this year, itself a small fraction of the total sugarcane standing on the Indian Ocean island, officials said on Tuesday.
"The damage caused to the sugarcane plantations is insignificant and estimated at five percent in respect of cane planted early this year," Mauritian Prime Minister Navin Ramgoolam told parliament.
Ramgoolam was referring to the plants known locally as "virgin canes", those planted this year and expected to be harvested for the first time next June.

An official of the Chamber of Agriculture (corrects from Ministry of Agriculture) said the sugarcane plants on average go through seven or eight regrowth cycles before they are replaced by virgin canes.
Most of the sugarcane plants in Mauritius have already been harvested at least once and are growing again for another cycle, officials of the sugar industry said.
At this period of year, these older plants are at their initial regrowth stage and were unaffected by cyclone Daniella, which hit the island on Sunday, they added.

The chamber official (corrects from "ministry official") said the damaged virgin canes are in central parts of the island and it was too early in the growth season to estimate how much sugar they would have produced.
In Mauritius, sugarcane is harvested between June and December and allowed to regrow during the rest of the year.
Mauritius produced 539,000 tonnes of sugar in 1995. REUTER MC JW
